# R354 — Native COPY opt-in decode host cost: source-path and observation audit

Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo). Read-only source audit of W HEAD `410904c/freeb54579c` in `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/diag-native-copy-queue-qualified-20261013`. No build, test, import, GPU/model/benchmark, process/service inspection, Git operation, reset, or source edit. Only this report was written. The supplied private `prefill-gemm-only-contract-root-v1/record.json` and broad environment were not read.

## Finding

With `STRATA_COPY_ENGINE=1`, ordinary decode does not create or submit work to the native copy-only queue. That queue is created from the prefill stager (`src/prefill/prefill.cpp:705`); decode's `token_stream` is either the generic main engine stream (`--stream-token`) or `nullptr` (`src/program/generate.cpp:3558-3563, 4901`). The native queue is still present in the same Runtime stream list and is subject to teardown/drain checks, but no decode call site found uses its pointer.

There is nevertheless a plausible opt-in host cost on compute submission. Every non-null `gpu::Stream` kernel path enters `compute_q(s) -> rt_of(s).stream(s)` (`src/core/gpu.cpp:93`). With opt-in off, `Runtime::stream` resolves and returns the queue. With opt-in on, it additionally calls `owner_of_stream(&queue)` and, if found, `owner->copy_only(&queue)` (`src/core/device.cpp:317-323`). For `nullptr`, this is still an added owner lookup on the current compute queue. For a same-runtime `main_cs` stream, `stream_for_copy` first checks `owns(q)` and then the guard performs a separate `owner_of_stream` scan. The latter takes the global runtime mutex and checks each initialized runtime/its queue list (`device.cpp:182-186`); `copy_only` takes the stream-list mutex and scans stream entries (`:309-315`). Thus the queue entry count and number of initialized devices can affect this CPU-side guard work. The code alone does not establish its duration or whether it is material against other decode work.

Native copy-only validation stays on copy/event/control paths: async memcpy routes through `q(s)`/`stream_for_copy` (`gpu.cpp:251-261,264-276`); event recording obtains the queue and copy-only state to reject timing tags and use a barrier (`:364-375`); checked finish drains a copy-only queue before release (`device.cpp:511-521`). The compute guard must remain for kernels, host tasks, graph and other compute operations. No candidate considered here removes or weakens that guard, event ordering, checked drain, ownership, or lifetime rule.

## Decode route and repeat counts

- Default token route (`stream_token=false`): `token_stream=nullptr` (`generate.cpp:4901`). Kernel wrappers using this route add the opt-in guard lookup against the current compute queue. Exact kernel wrapper count per generated token is backend/model/path dependent and cannot be derived reliably from the broad source search; do not multiply source call sites by layer count as an asserted total.
- `--stream-token`: all routed model work uses `main_cs`, created once as a normal stream (`generate.cpp:3558-3563,4901`). Each wrapper invocation has one `Runtime::stream` guard lookup after initial route resolution. The routine path for this one queue is not the native-copy stream.
- In the simple non-stream-token sampler loop, each generated position runs `sample_tokens(..., token_stream)` then a 4-byte `copy_async` and `stream_sync` (`generate.cpp:10588-10590`). `copy_async` uses `q`, not the compute guard; for `nullptr`, it adds no `owner_of_stream` scan, then stream sync with null resolves current runtime and queue directly. This separates copy route cost from kernel route cost.
- Default mode also calls `device_sync()` after the head and uses the logits D2H `copy_async` plus `stream_sync` when logits are read (`generate.cpp:10542-10556`). `--stream-token` skips the head-wide device sync and normally skips logits readback, but still samples and reads the token. These path changes are confounders if comparing modes; keep mode identical in COPY0/COPY1.
- A non-null stream path used by `event_record` performs queue ownership resolution and copy-role queries. It is not necessarily on the ordinary plain decode route. Copy/barrier submission count and compute guard lookup count should be recorded separately.

## Existing timing linkage and minimum observation

The immediate low-intrusion comparison is the user's quiet COPY0/1 standard benchmark with the same model/path, same generated-token count and conditions. Decode wall time is reported at `generate.cpp:11137-11142`; `--stats` already splits token host-visible phase intervals into PLE, embed, layers, head, readback, and sample (`:11191-11204`). The candidate lookup is exercised inside these phases, especially repeated kernel submissions through embed/layers/head/sample. These are wall-clock host call intervals that can include synchronous waits or asynchronous runtime submission work; they are not exclusive CPU time. They are sufficient to identify which phase's host-observed interval co-moves with total decode across quiet paired runs, but cannot attribute a delta specifically to the owner scan.

Minimum next diagnostic, only if the quiet pair shows a repeatable decode/phase delta worth localizing: add an opt-in diagnostic counter around the `Runtime::stream` opt-in guard, aggregated per decode run, with (a) number of guard calls, (b) total and max wall time spent in `owner_of_stream` and `copy_only` separately, and (c) which route class was checked (null/current compute, locally owned stream, remote-runtime stream). Keep the instrumentation disabled in the principal throughput rows; use a separate diagnostic pair because clock reads and counters perturb a very frequent path. Preserve all current guard/error semantics. Reconcile call counts and accumulated times with the existing `--stats` phase intervals, and report both totals without subtracting one from the other: the counters are nested within those intervals. A timer around whole `Runtime::stream` alone is insufficient to distinguish mutex/list lookup from the rest of route resolution. No additional profiler timeline is needed to answer this host lookup question.

A source-only fast-path candidate could avoid the second global ownership scan when the caller already has a trustworthy same-runtime queue identity, or cache immutable queue-role metadata, but queue identity/lifetime/remote-device semantics and concurrent stream insertion/destruction need a checked design. Source inspection is not proof that either is safe or valuable. Do not implement it from presumed list-scan cost. Measure first, and retain the rejection behavior for native copy-only queues on every compute route.

## Limits

This report establishes source-visible candidate work and relevant counters only. It does not measure call frequency, lock contention, nanoseconds, GPU effect, throughput impact, or a bottleneck. The observed COPY0/1 numbers supplied in the task are debug results and explicitly not adopted performance evidence; the main quiet comparison remains the appropriate first result. No tests/builds were run as instructed.
